newsitem.title: USA: J.P.Morgan flexes investment banking muscles.
newsitem.headline: J.P.Morgan flexes investment banking muscles.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc's third-quarter 1996 results Thursday offered convincing evidence the firm is now a power among the investment banks, with strong performance in underwriting and mergers & acquisitions advisory work.
"It's phenomenal," said George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison. "They've come from way down to being number four in underwriting in the U.S."
However a decline in trading revenues from record levels in the first half took some of the bloom off the rose.

Salem noted that trading revenues of $510 in the quarter just ended were up from $399 million in the comparable 1995 quarter, but down from $697 million in the second quarter of 1996. "A logical queston is, 'which is right?'," Salem said. The analyst cut his rating on J.P. Morgan to hold from buy.
Salomon Brothers analyst Diane Glossman left a hold rating intact but reduced earnings estimates for 1996 and 1997.
"Investment banking continues to show strong headway," she said.
Glossman said J.P. Morgan has shown again that it is a "real player" in the M&A advisory business.

For the third quarter of 1996, Securities Data Co ranked J.P. Morgan as the fourth-largest underwriter of U.S. debt and equtiy issues. The firm was lead manager on $19.2 billion in deals in the quarter, according to the tabulation.
Securities Data also had J.P. Morgan ranked sixth in completed M&A worldwide and fourth in pending transactions in the first nine months of 1996.
In the quarterly results, J.P. Morgan's investment banking revenue rose 19 percent from a year ago to $233 million.
Within investment banking, underwriting revenue rose to $83 million from $71 million a year ago and advisory and syndication fees rose to $150 million from $124 million.
Some major deals J.P. Morgan is currently working on have not closed but likely will buoy investment banking results in the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997.

The firm is advising Gillette Co in a planned acquisition of Duracell International Inc for about $7 billion and it is advising Star Enterprise, a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Saudi Aramco, which is talks with Shell Oil Co and Texaco Inc.

J.P. Morgan is also advising American Home Products Corp on a sale of an 80 percent stake in its food products unit. It is also adviser to Service Corp International in its hostile bid for Loewen Group Inc.

Analyst Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman noted that the $233 million in investment banking reveue topped the second quarter's record $210 million as well as an eight-quarter moving average of $137 million. He noted that advisory and syndication fees set a record at $150 million, while market conditions caused the underwriting revenue to slip to $83 million from $111 million in the second quarter.
